items.title: 美股繁榮是假象？AI泡沫疑慮升溫 標普500恐面臨30%修正
items.title_en: Is US Stock Market Prosperity an Illusion? AI Bubble Concerns Rise, S&P 500 May Face a 30% Correction
paras: 標普500指數10月中旬仍徘徊在7,600點上方高位區間，那斯達克與科技巨頭繼續主導市場敘事。表面繁榮之下，市場內部結構已出現深刻分化。前雷曼兄弟交易員、Bear Traps Report創辦人Larry McDonald提出的核心判斷——指數層面尚未充分反映的「內部崩盤」、被動投資的暗面、AI資本開支的不可持續性，以及硬資產與長久期債券的相對吸引力——在最新市場數據中得到部分印證，也引發對未來一至三年資產配置邏輯的重新審視。
當前市場最顯著的結構特徵是市值加權指數與多數成分股表現的嚴重背離。標普500中科技板塊權重長期接近或超過50%，前兩大權重股（輝達與蘋果）合計佔比一度接近13%。同時，大量知名品牌——Nike、麥當勞、家得寶、哈雷戴維森等消費與工業標的——自高點回落30%至80%。2026年10月中旬的市場數據繼續顯示，那斯達克與半導體板塊出現明顯調整，而指數整體仍維持相對韌性。

這種背離並非偶然。被動資金持續流入迫使指數基金與ETF不斷買入權重最大的少數股票，形成自我強化循環。當市場處於上漲年份且指數漲幅達到兩位數時，年末稅務損失賣出與機構調倉往往進一步加劇「強者恆強、弱者更弱」的格局。結果是：指數創下或接近歷史高位，而更廣泛的經濟與企業基本面卻已承壓。消費者層面，油價與中長期利率的顯著上行已構成實際購買力衝擊，連鎖消費與耐用品企業的業績與估值同步承壓，正是這一內部壓力的直接體現。
從歷史比較看，2000年科技泡沫與2007年金融危機前均出現過類似「指數掩蓋內部裂痕」的現象。當時權重集中度遠低於今日，而今日被動資金體量與算法交易的放大效應，使集中度風險更加突出。一旦權重股出現同步調整，指數層面的回撤可能遠超多數投資者的預期。
AI主題仍是驅動科技巨頭與指數的核心敘事，但資本開支的規模與回報週期已引發越來越多的質疑。超大規模科技公司與「新雲端」資料中心運營商持續大規模舉債與股權融資，用於算力、電力與土地投入。2026年下半年，部分資料中心相關債券與可轉債出現明顯拋售，CoreWeave等標的股價與信用利差同步惡化，被視為早期警示信號。

更深層的問題在於估值與退出機制。Anthropic、OpenAI等公司的估值從數年前的千億級躍升至數萬億級，一旦通過IPO或二級市場退出，零售與401(k)資金將在一定程度上成為接盤方。這與2000年前後科技股IPO潮存在結構性相似：早期投資者鎖定利潤，而後期進入者承擔更高估值風險。同時，AI相關資本開支對當期自由現金流形成顯著擠壓，部分巨頭從高自由現金流狀態轉向中性甚至負值，進一步放大了市場對「回報何時兌現」的疑慮。
輝達(NVDA-US)作為算力核心受益者，其估值與市值對指數影響巨大。晶片迭代加速、競爭加劇與客戶資本開支可能放緩，使未來兩到三年出現顯著估值回歸的概率上升。若這一情景兌現，指數層面30%級別的調整並非不可想象，而此後可能進入類似2000至2010年的長時間橫盤整理。
與股票市場形成鮮明對比的是債券市場的深度調整。2017至2021年超低利率環境下發行的大量長期公司債，在利率中樞顯著抬升後價格大幅下跌。以蘋果為例，部分低票息長期債券交易價格曾一度接近面值的一半。這類債券在利率回落情景下具備可觀的資本利得空間，疊加票息後的年化回報有望接近甚至超過部分股票的長期預期收益。
銀行業層面，商業地產貸款再融資壓力與低息存款流失風險並存。零利率時代積累的低成本存款在貨幣市場基金與穩定幣競爭下面臨流出壓力，進一步壓縮淨息差。歐洲銀行對主權債敞口的波動也提示全球固定收益市場的聯動風險。若長端利率出現階段性衝高後的反轉，長久期優質債券與國債有望成為重要的避險與收益來源。
長期來看，更高的通膨中樞與利率環境有利於控制實物資產的企業。1968至1981年高通膨與高利率週期中，工業、材料與能源在標普500中的權重曾達到約50%。當前這些板塊合計權重僅十餘個百分點。家庭財富中配置於商品與相關股票的比例也遠低於歷史高點。
銅、天然氣、石油服務與礦業公司不僅受益於AI資料中心與全球電力基礎設施建設，也受益於新興市場（尤其是印度）的能源與空調需求增長。即便AI資本開支出現階段性放緩，財富從高估值成長股向低估值硬資產的再配置本身就能提供支撐。自由現金流收益率較高、且持續回購的能源與材料公司，在風險回報比上往往優於高估值科技股。
黃金與白銀的表現進一步印證了這一邏輯。中央銀行持續購金、地緣政治不確定性與對主權信用的長期擔憂，使黃金在2026年維持高位運行。穩定幣規模已達約3,000億美元量級，其底層資產大量配置短期國債，客觀上增加了對美元短期債務的需求，卻也強化了金融壓抑與硬資產配置的吸引力。
美國聯邦債務規模龐大，單純依靠傳統手段難以持續。穩定幣的擴張、潛在的收益率曲線控制工具，以及黃金儲備的會計重估等「工具箱」選項，均指向某種形式的金融壓抑——通過機制設計壓低實際利率、引導資金進入特定資產。戰後初期聯準會與財政部的緊密協作提供了歷史參照。這類政策若落地，將進一步推動資金從純金融資產向硬資產與實物資產轉移。
同時，政治週期與中期選舉前後的政策不確定性，也可能成為市場波動的催化劑。無論是對AI資本開支的監管壓力，還是對財政可持續性的重新定價，都可能加速當前高度集中的市場結構發生調整。
在高度集中的市場環境下，單純持有市值加權指數已難以提供充分分散。等權重指數、主動構建的硬資產傾斜組合、精選長久期優質債券，以及具備資料護城河的細分AI應用領域（如醫療機器人、油氣服務資料平台），構成更具韌性的配置方向。稅務損失賣出後的反彈窗口、被過度拋售的優質品牌，也提供了階段性機會。
風險提示同樣明確：AI主題的調整若引發連鎖反應，可能短暫拖累硬資產需求預期；利率若繼續超預期上行，將加劇銀行業與消費端壓力；政策干預的力度與時點存在高度不確定性。投資者需在承認集中度風險的同時，避免簡單的全面做空，而應聚焦估值與現金流的相對優勢。
市場從不會以線性方式兌現風險。當前指數高位與內部裂痕並存的格局，更接近2000年前後的結構特徵，而非單一泡沫的簡單重演。被動投資的規模效應放大了權重股的影響力，也延緩了調整的全面展開。真正的風險不在於是否調整，而在於調整時投資者是否已提前完成從「指數跟隨」向「結構區分」的轉變。硬資產、現金流與合理估值，將成為下一階段更具確定性的錨點。
paras_en: The S&P 500 was still hovering above the 7,600‑point high‑range in mid‑October, while the Nasdaq and tech giants continued to dominate market narrative. Beneath the surface prosperity, the market’s internal structure has become sharply divided. Former Lehman trader and Bear Traps Report founder Larry McDonald’s core thesis – an “internal collapse” not yet reflected at the index level, the dark side of passive investing, the unsustainability of AI capital spending, and the relative appeal of hard assets and long‑duration bonds – finds partial confirmation in the latest data and prompts a reassessment of asset‑allocation logic for the next one to three years.

The most striking structural feature today is the severe divergence between the market‑cap‑weighted index and the performance of most constituents. The tech sector’s weight in the S&P 500 has long been near or above 50%, with the two largest holdings (Nvidia and Apple) at one point approaching 13% combined. At the same time, many well‑known consumer and industrial brands – Nike, McDonald’s, Home Depot, Harley‑Davidson and others – have fallen 30% to 80% from their peaks. Mid‑October 2026 data still show a clear pullback in the Nasdaq and semiconductor sector, while the overall index remains relatively resilient.

This divergence is not accidental. Ongoing inflows into passive funds force index funds and ETFs to keep buying the few highest‑weight stocks, creating a self‑reinforcing loop. In years when the market rises and the index posts double‑digit gains, year‑end tax‑loss selling and institutional rebalancing further amplify a “the strong get stronger, the weak get weaker” pattern. The result: the index reaches or nears historic highs while the broader economy and corporate fundamentals are under pressure. On the consumer side, higher oil prices and rising medium‑ to long‑term rates have eroded real purchasing power, squeezing chain‑store and durable‑goods companies’ earnings and valuations – a direct manifestation of this internal strain.

Historically, similar “index‑masking‑internal‑cracks” episodes appeared before the 2000 tech bubble and the 2007 financial crisis. Back then, weight concentration was far lower than today, but today’s massive passive capital and algorithmic‑trading amplification make concentration risk even more pronounced. If the heavyweight stocks adjust in sync, the index‑level drawdown could far exceed most investors’ expectations.

The AI theme still drives tech giants and the index, but the scale of capital spending and the length of payback periods are drawing increasing skepticism. Mega‑tech firms and “new‑cloud” data‑center operators continue to raise large amounts of debt and equity to fund compute, power and land. In the second half of 2026, some data‑center‑related bonds and convertibles saw noticeable selling; stocks such as CoreWeave and their credit spreads deteriorated, being viewed as early warning signs.

A deeper issue lies in valuations and exit mechanisms. Companies like Anthropic and OpenAI have seen valuations jump from the hundred‑billion to the tens‑of‑trillions dollar range in just a few years. If they exit via IPO or secondary markets, retail and 401(k) funds will become the buyers to some extent. This mirrors the tech‑IPO wave around 2000: early investors lock in profits while later entrants shoulder higher valuation risk. At the same time, AI‑related capex is squeezing current free‑cash‑flow, pushing some giants from strong free‑cash‑flow positions to neutral or even negative, heightening doubts about when returns will materialize.

Nvidia (NVDA‑US), as the core beneficiary of compute power, has an outsized impact on valuation and market‑cap weight. Accelerating chip cycles, intensifying competition and a possible slowdown in customer capex raise the probability of a significant valuation reversion over the next two to three years. If that scenario plays out, a 30%‑level correction at the index level is not unimaginable, after which the market could enter a prolonged sideways consolidation similar to 2000‑2010.

In stark contrast to equities, the bond market has undergone a deep correction. Long‑dated corporate bonds issued in the ultra‑low‑rate environment of 2017‑2021 have seen prices plunge sharply after central rates rose markedly. For example, some low‑coupon Apple long‑term bonds traded at roughly half of par. These bonds offer substantial capital‑gain potential if rates fall, and when combined with coupon yields their annualized return could approach or even exceed the long‑term expected returns of many stocks.

In banking, commercial‑real‑estate loan refinancing pressure coexists with the risk of low‑rate deposit outflows. Low‑cost deposits accumulated in the zero‑interest era face outflows to money‑market funds and stablecoins, further compressing net interest margins. European banks’ sovereign‑debt exposure volatility also highlights global fixed‑income linkage risk. Should long‑end rates spike and then reverse, high‑quality long‑duration bonds and sovereigns could become key hedges and return sources.

Over the long run, higher inflation cores and rate environments favor companies that control physical assets. During the high‑inflation, high‑rate cycle of 1968‑1981, industrials, materials and energy together accounted for about 50% of the S&P 500. Today those sectors together make up only a little over ten percent. The share of household wealth allocated to commodities and related equities is also far below historic peaks.

Copper, natural gas, oil‑service and mining firms benefit not only from AI data‑centers and global power‑infrastructure builds but also from growing energy and air‑conditioning demand in emerging markets, especially India. Even if AI capex eases temporarily, the reallocation of wealth from over‑valued growth stocks to undervalued hard assets can provide support. Energy and materials companies with high free‑cash‑flow yields and ongoing share buybacks often offer a better risk‑adjusted return than lofty‑valued tech stocks.

Gold and silver performance further validates this logic. Central‑bank gold purchases, geopolitical uncertainty and long‑term concerns about sovereign credit have kept gold near its 2026 highs. Stablecoin assets have reached roughly $300 billion, with underlying holdings heavily weighted to short‑term Treasuries, which objectively boosts demand for short‑term US debt while also reinforcing the appeal of financial repression and hard‑asset allocation.

The sheer size of US federal debt makes reliance on traditional tools unsustainable. The expansion of stablecoins, potential yield‑curve control mechanisms and accounting re‑valuation of gold reserves constitute a “toolbox” pointing toward a form of financial repression – designing mechanisms to push real rates lower and steer capital into specific assets. The close post‑World‑War‑II coordination between the Fed and Treasury offers a historical precedent. If such policies materialize, they would further shift capital from pure financial assets toward hard and real assets.

At the same time, political cycles and policy uncertainty around mid‑term elections can act as catalysts for market volatility. Whether through regulatory pressure on AI capex or a repricing of fiscal sustainability, such factors could accelerate adjustments in today’s highly concentrated market structure.

In a highly concentrated market environment, simply holding a market‑cap‑weighted index no longer provides adequate diversification. Equal‑weight indices, actively built hard‑asset‑tilted portfolios, carefully selected long‑duration high‑quality bonds, and niche AI applications with data moats (e.g., medical robotics, oil‑and‑gas service data platforms) represent more resilient allocation paths. Post‑tax‑loss‑sale rebound windows and oversold quality brands also offer tactical opportunities.

Risk warnings are clear: an AI‑theme correction that triggers a chain reaction could briefly dampen hard‑asset demand expectations; rates rising faster than expected would heighten pressure on banks and consumers; and the scale and timing of policy intervention remain highly uncertain. Investors should acknowledge concentration risk but avoid a blanket short‑sell approach, focusing instead on relative valuation and cash‑flow advantages.

Markets never realize risk in a linear fashion. The current coexistence of high index levels and internal cracks resembles the structural features of the early‑2000s rather than a simple replay of a single bubble. The scale effect of passive investing amplifies heavyweight influence and delays a full‑blown correction. The real risk lies not in whether a correction occurs, but whether investors have already shifted from “index‑following” to “structural‑distinction” before it does. Hard assets, cash flow and sensible valuations will become the next‑stage anchors of certainty.

paras_en: The dollar fell on Friday (the 16th), with both the euro and the yen posting their first weekly depreciation in more than a month, reflecting a cooling of market expectations for further Fed rate hikes and lingering investor worries that AI is weighing on equity markets.
In the New York close, the dollar index (DXY), which tracks the greenback against six major currencies, slipped 0.17% to 101.87, down about 0.35% for the week.

Consumer price and producer price data released this week came in above expectations, briefly unsettling markets. However, comments from Fed officials indicated no urgent need for further monetary tightening, helping to stabilise US Treasury yields and weakening support for the dollar.

AI‑related stocks fell sharply this week, and the pressure spread to parts of the credit market. Investors, who have heavily bet on every link of the AI supply chain, are now worried that data‑center operators may not generate profits quickly enough to service their debt.

Matt Weller, head of global market research at StoneX, said, "I think the most noteworthy phenomenon today and this week is the tight link between the dollar and AI trading. Usually when tech stocks are sold off, the market expects the dollar to strengthen on safe‑haven demand. We did see some flows into bonds, but the dollar actually fell."

The pound and the Swiss franc posted the biggest gains against the dollar this week. The franc was supported by safe‑haven demand, and markets expect that even if rates fall further, Switzerland is unlikely to push its policy rate below the current zero‑percent level.
The pound rose 0.31% to $1.3314, up 0.63% for the week.
The dollar slipped 0.25% against the Swiss franc to 0.8246 CHF, down 0.67% for the week. The franc had appreciated more than 1.4% over the past two trading days.
CME’s FedWatch tool shows the market now assigns an 83% probability that the Fed will keep rates unchanged later this month, up from 49% a month ago.
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh attended the IMF and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok on Friday and offered no clues about future rate decisions, saying he does not "pre‑judge" the outcome of any meeting.

John Velis, macro strategy strategist at BNY Mellon, said, "I think the Fed’s policy committee, especially the governors, have not yet reached sufficient consensus to support a rate hike in October. However, whether there will be a hike in December remains an open question, and many things could happen between now and then."
Euro‑area fiscal risks remain a focus.
Fiscal risk in France continues to be a background concern for markets, with French sovereign risk premiums spiking sharply in early October.
The euro rose 0.08% to $1.1227. It had gained 0.56% on Thursday, the biggest single‑day rise in two months, and is up about 0.23% for the week.

Investors expect that President Trump will try to avoid further escalation in the Middle East or Ukraine, as a larger conflict could push inflation higher and damage his political support ahead of the mid‑term elections.
The dollar fell 0.08% to ¥158.11, ending a four‑week streak of depreciation for the yen, which rose 0.13% this week. Previously, the Iran conflict had supported a stronger dollar.
Recent oil price gains have lifted the dollar while putting pressure on currencies of energy‑importing countries such as the euro and yen.
Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda reiterated on Friday that a potential inflation rate above the BOJ’s 2% target remains a risk to watch.

items.title_en: Taiwan Dollar Weakens While Stocks Hold, Falling 0.73 ¢ to Slip Below the 32.3 TWD Mark
paras: 在美元指數維持強勢、外資持續撤出亞洲市場影響下，新台幣兌美元今 (16) 日走弱，終場收在32.338元，貶值7.3分，續創近期波段低點，顯示國際資金仍偏向美元資產，相較於昨天的91億美元爆巨量，台北外匯經紀公司與元太外匯經紀公司合計總成交量為 46.12億美元。
儘管匯市承壓，台股表現相對有撐，加權指數終場收在47,111點，上漲141點，漲幅約0.3%，呈現匯弱股強格局。市場買盤主要聚焦 AI 伺服器、高階 PCB 及半導體供應鏈族群，在電子權值股支撐下，大盤成功守住漲勢。
從籌碼面來看，統計今日三大法人合計賣超約729億元，其中外資賣超高達494億元，已連續第8個交易日站在賣方；投信則持續扮演護盤角色，買超約132億元，寫下連6買；自營商賣超約367億元。
市場人士指出，本波新台幣轉弱主要受到美元升值效應帶動，近期美國經濟數據維持韌性，加上市場重新評估聯準會後續政策路徑，推升美元買盤，亞洲主要貨幣同步承壓，新台幣也不例外。資料顯示，10月以來新台幣已由31字頭一路走貶至32.3元以上水準。
觀察資金流向，外資近期持續調節台股權值股與電子類股部位，成為匯市與股市的重要變數。不過投信買盤明顯進場承接，加上AI相關產業基本面未見轉弱，因此支撐台股維持高檔震盪格局。今天市場呈現「匯率偏空、股市偏多」，除外資匯出導致台幣走弱，加上AI、高效能運算(HPC)及先進封裝需求仍強，吸引國內資金與長線買盤進駐，使台股維持相對強勢。
paras_en: Under a strong US dollar index and continued foreign‑capital outflows from Asian markets, the New Taiwan dollar weakened against the US dollar today (Oct 16), closing at 32.338 TWD, down 0.73 ¢ and extending its recent low‑point swing, indicating that international funds remain biased toward dollar assets. In contrast to yesterday’s massive USD 91 billion turnover, Taipei’s foreign‑exchange brokers and Yuan‑Tai FX brokers together handled a total volume of USD 46.12 billion.

Despite pressure on the currency market, Taiwan’s equity market showed relative resilience, with the weighted index closing at 47,111 points, up 141 points or about 0.3%, reflecting a “weak currency, strong stocks” pattern. Buying interest centered on AI servers, high‑end PCBs and semiconductor supply‑chain groups, and the rally in heavyweight electronics stocks helped the market maintain its upward momentum.

From a flow perspective, the three major institutional investors sold a combined net NT$729 billion today, with foreign investors leading the sell‑side at NT$494 billion for the eighth consecutive trading day. Trust funds continued to play a stabilising role, net‑buying about NT$132 billion for the sixth straight session, while proprietary traders sold roughly NT$367 billion.

Market observers said the recent weakening of the Taiwan dollar is mainly driven by the dollar’s appreciation. Recent US economic data remain resilient and the market’s reassessment of the Fed’s policy path has boosted dollar demand, putting pressure on major Asian currencies, including the TWD. Data show that since October the Taiwan dollar has slid from the low‑31s to above the 32.3 TWD level.

Looking at capital flows, foreign investors have been adjusting their positions in Taiwan’s heavyweight and electronics stocks, becoming a key variable for both the FX and equity markets. However, trust‑fund buying is evident, and the fundamentals of AI‑related industries have not weakened, supporting the Taiwan stock market’s high‑level range‑bound pattern. Today’s market displayed a “bearish currency, bullish equity” stance: foreign outflows weakened the TWD, while strong demand for AI, high‑performance computing and advanced packaging kept domestic and long‑term buying interest in equities, allowing the stock market to stay relatively strong.

paras: 美元周四(15日)自18個月高點回落，投資人將目光從強勁的美國通膨與消費支出數據，轉向 AI 資料中心業者債券遭拋售的情況。
紐約尾盤，追蹤美元兌六種主要貨幣的美元指數(DXY)下跌 0.45%，報 101.99。此前美國通膨數據高於預期，美元指數週三升至 18 個月高點。
美國 9 月生產者物價(PPI)以 4 年半來最快速度上漲，商品與服務成本同步增加，進一步顯示通膨壓力正從能源領域擴散至其他領域。
上個月零售銷售增幅高於預期，主要受到汽油價格上漲帶動，每週初領失業救濟金人數則小幅增加，顯示消費需求仍具韌性，勞動市場也維持穩定。
但美國公債價格上漲，美元則回落，反映聯準會(Fed)官員近期發表審慎言論，進一步降低市場對 10 月升息的預期。
Monex USA交易主管 Juan Perez 表示，「目前市場存在一種不利美元的論述，原因在於，通膨若維持在這樣的水準，且以如此快的速度上升，將難以持續。」
他表示，「無論戰事方面沒有好消息，或股市前景看起來悲觀，在過去四週美元大幅走強之後，市場仍傾向拋售美元……經濟停滯似乎對交易員的想法產生更大的影響。」
AI企業債務負擔受關注
美元回落帶動歐元反彈，歐元兌美元上漲 0.56%，從 18 個月低點升至 1.1218 美元，創下近兩個月來最大單日漲幅。
英鎊兌美元則上漲 0.64%，至 1.3275 美元，此前數據顯示，英國經濟 8 月意外成長 0.1%。
週三美國消費者物價指數（CPI）數據高於預期，最初推升市場對聯準會維持高利率更長時間的押注。同時，市場再度擔憂 AI 企業沉重的債務負擔，促使資金流向美國公債等避險資產，市場走勢因而震盪加劇。
Mesirow Currency Management 資深投資策略師 Uto Shinohara 表示，「晶片股遭拋售為債券提供支撐，使殖利率得以維持在相對受控的水準，抵銷通膨訊號帶來的影響。」
芝商所（CME Group）FedWatch 工具顯示，交易員目前預期，聯準會在 10 月 27 日至 28 日的會議上維持利率不變的機率為 73%，高於一個月前的 53%。
CPI 報告公布後，市場對升息的預期機率大幅上升，但聯準會負責監管事務的副主席鮑曼 (Michelle Bowman)，以及舊金山聯準銀行總裁戴莉 (Mary Daly) 等官員表示，聯準會可以等到會議前取得更明確的資訊再做決定，隨後市場對升息的押注便有所降溫。
LMAX Group 市場策略師 Joel Kruger 表示，「如果殖利率難以進一步走高，而美元每逢反彈便持續遭到賣出，將會強化我們的看法：通膨消息大致已被市場消化，風險的整體平衡將有利於風險性資產。」
投資人週五也將關注聯準會官員在曼谷舉行的國際貨幣基金（IMF）與世界銀行年度會議上的談話，包括聯準會主席華許 (Kevin Warsh)，以尋找美國央行下一步行動的線索。
澳幣兌美元下跌 0.77%，至 0.6919 美元，此前澳洲 9 月就業人數意外減少。
日元則升值 0.15%，至每美元兌 158.08 日元。
Shinohara 表示，「聯準會即將進入政策會議前的靜默期，而會議前也不再有一級重要經濟數據公布，因此市場走勢可能仍將受到俄羅斯與烏克蘭、伊朗相關地緣政治不確定性，以及 AI 產業發展的影響。」

paras_en: The dollar fell on Thursday (the 15th) from an 18‑month high as investors shifted their focus from strong U.S. inflation and consumer spending data to the sell‑off in bonds of AI data‑center operators.

In the New York close, the dollar index (DXY), which tracks the greenback against six major currencies, slipped 0.45% to 101.99. Earlier, U.S. inflation data came in above expectations, pushing the index to an 18‑month peak on Wednesday.

U.S. September producer prices (PPI) rose at the fastest pace in four and a half years, with costs for goods and services climbing together, further showing inflation pressure spreading from the energy sector to other areas.

Last month’s retail sales growth exceeded expectations, driven mainly by higher gasoline prices, while initial unemployment claims rose slightly, indicating consumer demand remains resilient and the labor market stays stable.
However, U.S. Treasury prices rose and the dollar retreated, reflecting recent cautious remarks from Federal Reserve officials that further lowered market expectations of a rate hike in October.

Juan Perez, head of trading at Monex USA, said, "There is currently a narrative that is unfavorable to the dollar because if inflation stays at this level and rises this quickly, it will be hard to sustain."

He added, "Whether there is no good news on the war front or the equity outlook looks bleak, after the dollar’s strong run over the past four weeks the market still tends to sell the greenback… stagnation seems to have a bigger impact on traders’ thinking."
AI companies' debt burdens draw attention
The dollar’s decline lifted the euro, which rose 0.56% against the dollar from an 18‑month low to $1.1218, marking the biggest single‑day gain in nearly two months.
The pound rose 0.64% to $1.3275 after data showed the U.K. economy unexpectedly grew 0.1% in August.

Wednesday’s U.S. consumer price index (CPI) came in above expectations, initially boosting bets that the Fed would keep rates high for longer. At the same time, renewed worries about heavy debt loads at AI firms prompted a flow into safe‑haven assets such as U.S. Treasuries, intensifying market volatility.

Uto Shinohara, senior investment strategist at Mesirow Currency Management, said, "The sell‑off in chip stocks provided support for bonds, keeping yields at relatively controlled levels and offsetting the impact of inflation signals."
The CME Group FedWatch tool shows traders now assign a 73% probability that the Fed will leave rates unchanged at its Oct. 27‑28 meeting, up from 53% a month ago.

After the CPI report, the market’s probability of a rate hike surged, but Fed Vice‑Chair Michelle Bowman and San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said the Fed could wait for clearer information before deciding, cooling the market’s rate‑hike bets.

LMAX Group market strategist Joel Kruger said, "If yields struggle to rise further and the dollar keeps getting sold each time it rebounds, it reinforces our view that inflation news has largely been priced in and the overall risk balance will favor risky assets."
Investors will also watch Friday for comments from Fed officials at the IMF and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, including Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, for clues on the central bank’s next move.
The Australian dollar fell 0.77% to $0.6919 after September job numbers in Australia unexpectedly dropped.
The yen appreciated 0.15% to 158.08 per dollar.

Shinohara noted, "The Fed is entering a pre‑meeting quiet period, and no major economic data will be released before the meeting, so market moves may still be influenced by geopolitical uncertainties related to Russia, Ukraine, Iran, and the development of the AI industry."

items.title: 〈台幣〉股匯雙殺再現！匯市爆91億美元巨量 重摔近2角收32.265元
items.title_en: Taiwan Dollar Faces Dual Stock‑Currency Slump Again! FX Market Swells to $9.115 Billion, Drops Nearly 2 ¢ to 32.265
paras: 台北外匯市場今(15)日上演股匯雙殺戲碼，在外資大舉撤出、台股重挫逾千點衝擊下，新台幣兌美元匯率終場收在32.265元，重貶1.92角，成交金額更放大至 91.15 億美元，顯示市場避險情緒急遽升溫。今日外資及陸資單日淨賣超逾3000億元，成新台幣重貶的最大主因。
新台幣今日以32.11元開出後一路走弱，盤中最低來到32.452元，最低一度崩跌 3.79 角，終場收32.265元，改寫逾 2 個月新低。台北及元太外匯市場總成交量爆出 91.15 億美元的天量，直接打破歷史單日最高成交量紀錄。
匯銀人士指出，今日新台幣走勢主要受到外資大規模匯出影響，而背後關鍵則來自台股出現恐慌性賣壓。市場憂心全球科技股修正及資金風險偏好下降，導致外資同步在股市與匯市進行調節。
觀察今日台股表現，加權指數終場收在46969.87點，大跌1655.96點，跌幅達3.41%，成交值約新台幣1.43兆元，市場氣氛急速轉弱。
法人動向更顯示資金撤離力道驚人。根據證交所統計，三大法人今日合計賣超3700.76億元，其中外資及陸資賣超3025.55億元，自營商賣超958.24億元，僅投信逆勢買超283.03億元。進一步觀察，外資及陸資今日賣出金額高達6773.6億元，遠高於買進的3748.05億元，單日淨賣超逾3000億元，成為新台幣重貶的重要推手。
市場人士分析，近期美元續獲避險資金青睞，加上美債殖利率維持高檔，使亞洲貨幣普遍承壓。加上台股面臨外資調節電子權值股壓力，連帶新台幣跌勢較區域貨幣更加明顯。且今日匯市成交量明顯放大至逾91億美元，遠高於一般交易日水準，反映出口商、進口商及外資同步進場調節部位。
從技術面觀察，新台幣近期持續在32元整數關卡附近震盪，今日收盤已回落至32.265元，代表市場短線仍以美元需求為主。若後續外資持續匯出，不排除匯價仍有測試32.3元至32.5元區間的可能。
今日股匯市同步大幅震盪，也凸顯國際資金流向已成為牽動台灣金融市場的關鍵因素，後續外資是否止血，將成為觀察新台幣能否穩住32元關卡的重要指標。
paras_en: Taipei’s foreign‑exchange market staged a double‑whammy of stocks and currency today (15th), as foreign investors pulled out en masse and the Taiwan stock index plunged over a thousand points. The New Taiwan dollar closed at 32.265 per US dollar, a depreciation of 1.92 ¢, with transaction volume ballooning to $9.115 billion, indicating a sharp rise in market hedging sentiment. Foreign and mainland Chinese investors posted a net sell‑off of more than NT$300 billion for the day, the main driver of the dollar’s steep fall.

The New Taiwan dollar opened at 32.11 and weakened throughout the session, hitting a low of 32.452, a drop of 3.79 ¢ at its deepest point, and closed at 32.265, breaking a more‑than‑two‑month low. The Taipei and Yuan‑Tai foreign‑exchange markets together recorded a record‑high daily turnover of $9.115 billion, shattering the previous single‑day volume record.

Currency‑bank officials said the dollar’s move was mainly driven by massive foreign‑exchange outflows from overseas investors, with the underlying cause being panic selling in the Taiwan stock market. The market fears a correction in global tech stocks and a decline in risk appetite, prompting foreign investors to adjust positions in both equities and FX simultaneously.

Looking at today’s stock performance, the weighted index closed at 46,969.87 points, down 1,655.96 points or 3.41%, with a turnover of about NT$1.43 trillion, reflecting a rapid weakening of market sentiment.

Institutional flows further highlight the magnitude of capital outflows. According to exchange statistics, the three major institutional groups sold a combined NT$370.076 billion today, with foreign and mainland Chinese investors net‑selling NT$302.555 billion and proprietary traders selling NT$95.824 billion, while only investment trusts bought a net NT$28.303 billion. More specifically, foreign and mainland Chinese investors sold NT$677.36 billion versus purchases of NT$374.805 billion, a net daily sell‑off of over NT$300 billion, becoming a key force behind the dollar’s sharp depreciation.

Market analysts note that the US dollar continues to attract safe‑haven flows, and US Treasury yields remain high, putting pressure on Asian currencies. Coupled with foreign investors trimming exposure to Taiwan’s heavy‑weight electronic stocks, the New Taiwan dollar has weakened more than regional peers. Today’s FX turnover surged past $9.1 billion, far above normal trading‑day levels, reflecting exporters, importers and foreign investors all adjusting positions together.

From a technical perspective, the New Taiwan dollar has been oscillating around the 32.00 mark. Today’s close at 32.265 suggests short‑term market demand remains dollar‑driven. If foreign outflows persist, further testing of the 32.30‑32.50 range cannot be ruled out.

The simultaneous large swings in stocks and FX today underscore that international capital flows have become a pivotal driver of Taiwan’s financial markets. Whether foreign investors can halt the outflow will be a key gauge for the dollar’s ability to hold the 32.00 level going forward.

items.title: 瑞銀維持美元「逢低買進」策略
items.title_en: UBS Maintains "Buy the Dip" Strategy for the Dollar
paras: 《Investing.com》報導，瑞銀(UBS)週三(14日)在給客戶的報告中表示，只要能源價格維持高檔，且AI投資題材持續發酵，逢美元回檔時買進仍是合適的策略。
策略師Shahab Jalinoos表示，G10貨幣市場本週走勢相對平淡，法國與德國10年期公債殖利率利差穩定在約140個基點。
他指出，從法國的角度來看，這個利差水準仍令人不安，也持續支持歐元兌美元應採取「逢高賣出」策略的觀點。
瑞銀預期，歐元將測試第四季的區間低點1.1050，並維持2026年底目標價1.1200不變。
Jalinoos指出，柴油價格可能接近穩定的初步跡象，為歐元提供部分支撐。然而，歐洲仍面臨風險，天然氣庫存處於異常低檔，天然氣期貨價格也升至本輪週期新高。
近期科技股走勢疲軟，可能促使美元進入部分整理階段，通膨數據也可能進一步降低市場對未來較長期間升息的預期。
他寫道，「儘管如此，我們的核心觀點仍未改變：只要能源價格維持高檔，且AI帶動的投資題材持續發酵，逢美元走低時買進仍是合適的策略。」
在商品貨幣方面，瑞銀認為，澳幣、紐幣與加幣目前處於整理階段，但由於市場對升息的定價有限，這三種貨幣都有機會收復9月的跌幅。其中，加幣是瑞銀最偏好的短線做多標的。
Jalinoos也反駁了「日本減持法國債券將推升日元」的看法。他表示，國際收支數據顯示，日本對法國債券的曝險部位已大幅下降。
paras_en: Investing.com reported that UBS on Wednesday (the 14th) said in a client report that as long as energy prices stay high and AI‑related investment themes keep developing, buying the dollar on dips remains an appropriate strategy.
Strategist Shahab Jalinoos noted that G10 currency markets were relatively flat this week, with the spread between French and German 10‑year government bond yields steady at about 140 basis points.
He pointed out that from a French perspective this spread level is still unsettling and continues to support the view that the euro versus the dollar should be sold on rallies.
UBS expects the euro to test the fourth‑quarter low of 1.1050 and keeps its year‑end‑2026 target unchanged at 1.1200.

Jalinoos said diesel prices may be showing early signs of stabilisation, offering some support to the euro. However, Europe still faces risks as natural‑gas inventories are at unusually low levels and gas futures have risen to a new high for this cycle.
Weakness in recent tech stocks could push the dollar into a partial correction, and inflation data may further reduce market expectations for prolonged rate hikes.

He wrote, "Nevertheless, our core view remains unchanged: as long as energy prices stay high and AI‑driven investment themes continue to develop, buying the dollar on its declines remains an appropriate strategy."

Regarding commodity currencies, UBS sees the Australian, New Zealand and Canadian dollars as currently in a consolidation phase, but with limited rate‑hike pricing in the market each has a chance to recover September losses. The Canadian dollar is UBS’s top short‑term long‑biased pick.

Jalinoos also rebutted the view that Japan’s reduction of French bond holdings would boost the yen, noting that balance‑of‑payments data show Japan’s exposure to French bonds has already fallen sharply.

週三德勤(Deloitte)調查英國企業首席財務官(CFO)預計一年後通貨膨脹率升至3.4%及認為信貸成本高昂的比例創兩年半新高，而且法國財政問題衝擊歐元兌英鎊至十六個月新低，推升英鎊兌美元至1.3275高點。隨著英國央行(BOE)首席經濟學家皮爾稱市場對BOE未來一年加息四次、每次25個基點的推測過於激進，在美國CPI數據後，重創英鎊兌美元至1.3132低點。預估今日英鎊兌美元阻力於1.3230-50，支撐於1.3130-50。

New York Fed President Williams said there is no need for further rate hikes next year, and Boston Fed President Collins added that Fed officials are aware that rising rates could create problems for financial institutions. Moreover, Japanese Finance Ministry Vice‑Minister Mikami Jun said at the IMF‑World Bank meetings that ASEAN countries face urgent energy‑shock and inflation challenges and that Japan should also provide fiscal support. Japanese importers and speculators buying dollars have pushed USD/JPY higher.

paras: 美元周三(14日)觸及至18個月高點，美國通膨數據強於預期，一度重新點燃市場對聯準會(Fed)可能在本月稍晚升息的預期。不過，隨著投資人重新預期聯準會將保持耐心，美元隨後自高點回落。
紐約尾盤，追蹤美元兌六種主要貨幣的美元指數(DXY)上漲0.34%，報102.53，稍早在上午尾盤一度升至102.94。
美國勞工部勞工統計局公布的數據顯示，由於汽油價格大幅上漲，美國9月消費者物價明顯攀升。
State Street資深全球市場策略師Marvin Loh表示，「CPI數據仍在影響市場估值，而股市下跌又提供了另一個推升美元的理由。」
這份通膨報告蓋過了聯準會官員近期釋出的鴿派訊號，包括紐約聯準銀行總裁威廉斯(John Williams)的言論。他的評論曾在前一個交易日導致美元走弱。
聯準會負責監管事務的副主席鮑曼(Michelle Bowman)週四也釋出訊號，表示在再次升息之前，將採取觀望態度。
另一方面，聯準會週三公布的「褐皮書」顯示，美國勞動市場仍處於「低聘僱、低解僱」狀態，但部分地區的通膨壓力有所升高。
Mesirow Currency Management資深投資策略師Uto Shinohara表示，「聯準會的雙重使命與勞動市場疲弱的跡象之間，仍存在拉鋸。明天公布的零售銷售、初領失業救濟金人數及生產者物價指數(PPI)，應能讓我們更清楚掌握消費者狀況、勞動市場與物價壓力。」
芝商所(CME Group)的FedWatch工具顯示，交易員目前預期聯準會在10月27日至28日的會議上維持利率不變的機率為65%，高於一個月前的53%。市場預期截至2027年底，累計緊縮幅度約為79個基點。
美國央行上個月將政策利率調升0.25個百分點，使利率區間升至3.75%至4.00%。
Angeles Investments投資長Michael Rosen表示，投資人對美國是否願意採取行動抑制通膨，正逐漸失去信心。
Rosen表示，「我們看到……美元走強受到較高利率的支撐。除非聯準會大幅升息、促使經濟陷入衰退，或是我們修正貿易與移民政策，否則通膨不會下降。」
歐元面臨壓力
多國財政與金融主管目前齊聚曼谷，出席國際貨幣基金(IMF)與世界銀行(World Bank)的年度會議。
IMF財政事務主管Rodrigo Valdes表示，IMF已提高對各國政府控制不斷攀升債務的呼籲力度。IMF總裁Kristalina Georgieva則表示，美國需要進行財政調整，讓債務走上更可持續的道路。
法國公債是近期全球債券拋售潮中受衝擊最嚴重市場之一。投資人擔心，明年總統大選前的政治角力，可能阻礙法國降低高額財政赤字的努力。
歐洲央行(ECB)總裁拉加德(Christine Lagarde)在曼谷出席CNN活動時表示，法國應透過財政整頓解決債務問題。這番言論降低了市場對歐洲央行可能開始買進法國公債、以壓低殖利率的猜測。
由於油價上漲，加上市場持續擔憂法國的財政狀況，歐元進一步承壓。
歐元下跌0.41%，至1.1152美元，兌美元匯率創下17個月新低，兌英鎊則跌至16個月新低。
UniCredit外匯策略師Roberto Mialich表示，歐元短期內可能測試1.10美元，但對年底前的歐元走勢，他的看法沒有那麼悲觀。他預期，「美國公債殖利率可能回落，儘管歐元區情勢仍可能對歐元構成壓力。」
《金融時報》週三報導，英國財政大臣John Healey預計，本月預算案中所有新增的支出措施，都將透過加稅或削減支出來支應，而非增加借款。
IMF一名高階官員表示，該機構並未建議英國加快財政整頓的步伐。

paras_en: The dollar hit an 18‑month high on Wednesday (the 14th) as U.S. inflation data came in stronger than expected, briefly reigniting market expectations that the Federal Reserve might raise rates later this month. However, as investors revised their outlook to see the Fed staying patient, the dollar retreated from its peak.
In the New York close, the dollar index (DXY), which tracks the greenback against six major currencies, rose 0.34% to 102.53, after having briefly climbed to 102.94 earlier in the session.
Data released by the U.S. Labor Department’s Bureau of Labor Statistics showed that September’s consumer price index rose sharply, driven by a large jump in gasoline prices.
State Street senior global markets strategist Marvin Loh said, “CPI data is still influencing market valuations, and the stock market decline provides another reason to push the dollar higher.”

The inflation report eclipsed recent dovish signals from Fed officials, including comments from New York Fed President John Williams, whose remarks had weakened the dollar on the previous trading day.
Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman also signaled on Thursday that the central bank would adopt a wait‑and‑see stance before any further rate hikes.
Meanwhile, the Fed’s Beige Book released on Wednesday showed that the U.S. labor market remains in a “low‑hiring, low‑layoff” environment, though inflation pressures have risen in some regions.

Mesirow Currency Management senior investment strategist Uto Shinohara said, “The Fed’s dual mandate is still at odds with signs of a weakening labor market. Tomorrow’s retail sales, initial jobless claims and producer price index (PPI) data should give us a clearer picture of consumer conditions, the labor market and price pressures.”

CME Group’s FedWatch tool shows traders now assign a 65% probability that the Fed will keep rates unchanged at its Oct. 27‑28 meeting, up from 53% a month ago. The market expects a cumulative tightening of about 79 basis points by the end of 2027.
The U.S. central bank raised its policy rate by 0.25 percentage point last month, moving the target range to 3.75%‑4.00%.
Angeles Investments chief investment officer Michael Rosen said investors are losing confidence that the United States will take decisive action to curb inflation.

Rosen added, “We see the dollar’s strength being supported by higher rates. Unless the Fed hikes aggressively enough to push the economy into recession, or we overhaul trade and immigration policy, inflation won’t come down.”
Euro Under Pressure
Finance and central‑bank leaders from multiple countries are gathered in Bangkok for the International Monetary Fund and World Bank annual meetings.

IMF finance chief Rodrigo Valdes said the Fund has stepped up its calls for governments to rein in soaring debt. IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva added that the United States needs fiscal adjustments to put its debt on a more sustainable path.

French sovereign bonds have been among the hardest hit in the recent global bond sell‑off. Investors worry that political battles ahead of next year’s presidential election could hamper France’s efforts to reduce its large fiscal deficit.

European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde, speaking at a CNN event in Bangkok, said France should address its debt problem through fiscal consolidation. Her remarks dampened market speculation that the ECB might start buying French bonds to lower yields.
Higher oil prices and continued concerns about France’s fiscal health have added further pressure on the euro.
The euro fell 0.41% to $1.1152, hitting a 17‑month low against the dollar and a 16‑month low against the pound.

UniCredit foreign‑exchange strategist Roberto Mialich said the euro could test $1.10 in the short term, but he is less pessimistic about its trajectory by year‑end, expecting “U.S. Treasury yields may retreat even though euro‑area conditions could still weigh on the euro.”

The Financial Times reported on Wednesday that UK Treasury Secretary John Healey expects all new spending announced in this month’s budget to be funded by tax hikes or cuts rather than additional borrowing.
An IMF senior official said the institution has not advised the United Kingdom to accelerate its fiscal consolidation pace.
The pound slipped 0.59% to $1.3177.
The dollar fell 0.08% against the yen, to ¥158.16.
